title: Earthquake Swarm Rattles Sipí and Istmina, Reactivating Chocó Alert Five Weeks After M7.4 Quake
detail: Colombia's National Seismological Network recorded at least seven tremors on September 14 (magnitude 3.2–4.9, depths 39–120 km) centered on Sipí and Istmina in Chocó's San Juan region, felt as far as Valle del Cauca, Risaralda, Antioquia and Tolima with more than 2,000 'did you feel it' reports by mid-afternoon. Network coordinator Freddy Tovar classified the activity as a genuine 'earthquake swarm' — a sequence lacking a single mainshock from which aftershocks progressively decrease — rather than standard aftershocks of the August 10 M7.4 quake. More than 1,340 tremors have been registered in the area since August 10, reviving anxiety in communities still housed in temporary shelters more than a month after the disaster.

media.caption: Chocó continues to shake more than a month after the magnitude-7.4 earthquake

title: Bogotá Judge Orders Ministry of Defense to Disclose Full Presidential Flight Records
detail: Bogotá's Ninth Specialized Criminal Circuit Court ruled that the Ministry of Defense, led by retired General Jorge Eduardo Mora, had violated the rights of Pacto Histórico Representative José Luis Bohórquez López by supplying only partial flight records (Aug 7–24) in response to his request, and ordered complete disclosure — including the August 25–September 8 window — within 48 hours. Bohórquez's initial data found roughly COP 1.117 billion (≈US$353,500) spent on presidential flights across just 18 days, including 36 helicopter flights under six minutes connecting a Barranquilla sports facility to the airport. The ruling escalated a transparency fight over de la Espriella's travel costs one month into his term; as of September 19 the government had not issued a detailed response to the disclosed figures.

media.caption: A Bogotá judge ordered full disclosure of President de la Espriella's flight costs
